findings.paper_title: Information & Monitoring Arrangements of West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) Arm's Length Companies Annual Update
findings.headline: Annual monitoring reports to Audit Committee established for portfolio of 8 arm's length companies across transport, investment, and infrastructure
findings.detail: WMCA has established annual monitoring reports to the Audit, Risk & Assurance Committee covering eight arm's length companies (Midland Metro Limited, West Midlands Growth Company, investment funds, West Midlands Development Capital, 5G deployment, and rail operations). The framework sets out director appointment protocols, conflict of interest management, and shareholder oversight responsibilities.
findings.matters: Finance directors overseeing multiple arm's length companies need systematic monitoring to surface problems early. The BCIMO failure demonstrates the need; this framework shows how WMCA is attempting to catch issues across a complex portfolio.
findings.figures: 8 companies/entities in portfolio
findings.quote: Prepare an annual monitoring report for ARAC to be brought to the last meeting of each municipal year. This is deemed good governance to ensure there is sufficient oversight of the WMCA's companies.

findings.paper_title: Information & Monitoring Arrangements of West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) Arm's Length Companies Annual Update
findings.headline: Joint venture with Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council placed in administration; dissolution application filed 10 July 2026
findings.detail: Black Country Innovative Manufacturing Organisation (BCIMO), a research and technology organisation jointly owned with Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council, has been placed into administration. An application has been filed at Companies House to move from administration to dissolution. WMCA's liability was limited to £1.
findings.matters: Corporate failures in arm's length company portfolios show the risks inherent in using separate legal entities; finance directors at peer councils managing similar structures need to understand what went wrong to avoid recurrence.
findings.figures: Liability limited to £1; application filed 10 July 2026
findings.quote: This company was placed into administration. On 10 July 2026, an application was filed at Companies House to move from administration to dissolution.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Information & Monitoring Arrangements of West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) Arm's Length Companies Annual Update
findings.headline: Brownfield Housing Fund will not be extended beyond December 2026
findings.detail: Ian Martin, who oversees the Brownfield Housing Fund, does not intend to seek an extension beyond the end of 2026. The fund will therefore cease operation at the end of 2026.
findings.matters: The wind-down of a funding programme signals a change in WMCA's commitment to brownfield housing delivery and affects plans of partner organisations.
findings.figures: December 2026
findings.quote: Ian Martin is responsible for overseeing this fund but does not intend to seek an extension beyond December 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Information & Monitoring Arrangements of West Midlands Combined Authority (WMCA) Arm's Length Companies Annual Update
findings.headline: Friars Park joint venture agreement is being renegotiated with key changes to how development proceeds will be split
findings.detail: A change request approved by Investment Board in 2024 to vary the Friars Park JV Agreement is well progressed and close to being finalised. The key changes relate to how development proceeds will be split between WMCA and Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council. SMBC is the lead project manager and Keepmoat has been appointed as development partner.
findings.matters: Changes to the proceeds-sharing mechanism in a major development project directly affect WMCA's financial returns and investment outcomes.
findings.figures: No project value or split percentages disclosed

findings.paper_title: Assurance Performance Report - Q1 2026/27 (April - June 2026)
findings.headline: Compressed assurance reviews increased to three in Q1, reducing formal governance oversight of devolved funding projects.
findings.detail: Compressed Assurance and Appraisal Reviews combine both review processes into a single review and are used for low-risk projects or where accelerated decisions are needed. Three were conducted in Q1 compared to two in Q4. The paper explicitly flags this approach 'reduces the risk mitigation that the SAF provides', indicating that formal governance oversight is compromised when the standard assurance process is compressed.
findings.matters: Compressed reviews bypass elements of the formal assurance framework designed to provide independent oversight of devolved investment projects, relevant to lenders and governance stakeholders monitoring controls over public funds.
findings.figures: three Compressed Assurance and Appraisal Reviews were conducted, compared to two in the previous quarter
findings.quote: The risk flagged in 11.3 relates to the compressed Assurance and Appraisal review activity which reduces the risk mitigation that the SAF provides.

findings.paper_title: Assurance Performance Report - Q1 2026/27 (April - June 2026)
findings.headline: Only 34% of anticipated business cases delivered on time in Q1 2026/27, with 66% of expected cases not yet received.
findings.detail: Of 59 business cases forecast for Q1, only 20 were received as planned; 39 remain outstanding. Transport projects account for the majority of delays, driven by the impact of the Rosewell review and CRSTS programme reprofiling. The report states delays 'could affect the timing and profiling of future expenditure, resource requirements, and delivery trajectories' and will be monitored for impacts on capital and revenue forecasts. The Executive Board is managing this as a known risk with a Portfolio Management Office being established to coordinate activity.
findings.matters: Business case delays affect the timing and deployment of devolved investment funding and achievement of programme delivery outcomes, key metrics for finance directors and lenders monitoring programme performance and cash flows.
findings.figures: 20 (34%) were received as planned; 39 anticipated business cases (66%) have not yet been received
findings.quote: Of the 59 business cases anticipated for the quarter, only 20 (34%) were received as planned during the reporting period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: Audit identifies insufficient resourcing, capacity and requisite skillsets as key constraints to resolving DBS control weaknesses
findings.detail: The audit report identifies that insufficient resourcing, capacity and requisite skillsets represent key constraints that should be addressed as a priority to resolve the identified control weaknesses. The lack of training for People Service Centre staff dealing with DBS checks was specifically flagged as requiring urgent attention.
findings.matters: When an audit identifies resourcing and capacity as a blocker to fixing control weaknesses, it signals to external stakeholders that the council understands what needs to be fixed but cannot access the resources to do it, raising questions about overall operational capacity.
findings.figures: 70 posts requiring DBS checks; audit scope covered testing from April 2025 to February 2026
findings.quote: Insufficient resourcing, capacity, and requisite skillsets represent key constraints and should be addressed as a priority to facilitate the resolution of these weaknesses.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: DBS Update Service not in use and system to automatically flag expiring DBS certificates has not been implemented
findings.detail: The council has not yet implemented the DBS Update Service, which would allow certificates to be kept current and employers to check certificate status without requesting new DBS checks. Additionally, the planned addition of DBS check dates to the Business World system to generate expiry alerts has not been implemented. Without these controls, the council currently lacks a systematic way to identify when DBS recertification is required.
findings.matters: DBS certificates are only accurate on the day issued; without tracking and systematic flagging of expiry dates, the council risks staff continuing to work in regulated roles with expired or expiring clearance.
findings.figures: Affects 70 posts identified as requiring DBS checks
findings.quote: The DBS update service is not yet in use and the planned addition of DBS check dates to the Business World system to set expiry alerts is also not yet in place.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: One employee identified as having commenced a seconded role without required DBS clearance first being obtained
findings.detail: Testing identified an instance where an employee started a seconded role without the required DBS check being completed and cleared beforehand. This represents a direct breach of the council's own DBS process and indicates that the controls over process compliance were not operating effectively.
findings.matters: Allowing an individual to work in a role requiring DBS clearance before clearance is obtained is a compliance breach and a safeguarding risk that both regulators and external stakeholders assessing organisational controls would view seriously.
findings.figures: 1 instance identified in testing of sample from April 2025 to February 2026
findings.quote: There was an instance identified whereby an employee commenced their seconded role without the required DBS clearance first being in place;

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: Contract with Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council for basic DBS checks lacks key terms including deliverables, duration and termination arrangements
findings.detail: The contract with BMBC for basic DBS checks is incomplete, missing critical components including deliverables, contract duration, and termination arrangements. This leaves the contractual arrangement poorly defined and gives the council limited contractual levers to manage the relationship or enforce service standards.
findings.matters: Outsourced contracts require clear terms around scope, duration, and exit provisions; their absence indicates weak contract management that could affect service continuity.
findings.figures: 70 posts identified as requiring DBS checks
findings.quote: The contract in place with Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council (BMBC) to provide all basic DBS checks did not include a number of key components such as deliverables, duration and termination arrangements;

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: No contract found between WMCA and Coventry City Council for standard and enhanced DBS check provision
findings.detail: The audit could not locate or identify any contract between WMCA and Coventry City Council (CCC) for the provision of standard and enhanced DBS checks. This represents a significant contractual gap, as CCC has been the provider for these services without any documented contractual arrangement in place to govern the relationship.
findings.matters: Outsourcing a critical safeguarding function without a formal contract leaves both parties exposed and limits the council's ability to enforce service levels, performance standards, or exercise termination rights.
findings.figures: CCC provides standard and enhanced DBS checks; 70 posts identified as requiring DBS checks
findings.quote: No contract could be located/provided between Coventry City Council (CCC) and WMCA for the provision of all standard and enhanced DBS checks;

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Corporate Risk Register
findings.headline: Delivering transformation scored 16 against target of 4, indicating poor benefit realisation
findings.detail: The risk that increasing resources in infrastructure, people and processes are not managed effectively, resulting in duplication of effort and missed delivery opportunities, is rated at likelihood 4/5 and impact 4/5 for a total score of 16. The target is only 4, showing the actual risk is significantly above acceptable.
findings.matters: A transformation programme failing to deliver value whilst consuming significant capital and revenue resources directly impacts financial return on investment.
findings.figures: Likelihood 4, Impact 4, Total score 16, Target score 4
findings.quote: Fails to maximise best use of increasing resources; investments in infrastructure, people and processes are not managed to reduce contradiction and duplication of effort, minimise delivery gaps, or exploit new business models

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Corporate Risk Register
findings.headline: TfWM capital delivery risk scored 20 against target of 8
findings.detail: The risk of failure to deliver capital activity on time and in budget across the transport portfolio is rated at likelihood 4/5 and impact 5/5, producing a total score of 20. The register identifies an increase in parallel delivery requirements across the region within a constrained timeframe, intensifying this risk.
findings.matters: Capital delivery failure would delay regional transport investment and impair the authority's ability to execute its strategic priorities.
findings.figures: Likelihood 4, Impact 5, Total score 20, Target score 8
findings.quote: Failure to deliver capital activity on time and in budget across the transport portfolio (regional) and an increase in requirements to deliver in parallel across the region in the remaining timeframe.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Corporate Risk Register
findings.headline: Cybersecurity risk scored 20 against target of 9, well above acceptable level
findings.detail: The risk of cybersecurity breach or internal failure causing unauthorised data disclosure or financial manipulation is rated at likelihood 5/5 and impact 4/5, producing a total score of 20. The target is 9, indicating the actual risk is significantly above where the organisation intends it to be.
findings.matters: A material gap between target and actual risk in critical infrastructure protection indicates insufficient control investment or remediation of known vulnerabilities.
findings.figures: Likelihood 5, Impact 4, Total score 20, Target score 9
findings.quote: Cybersecurity breach by a third-part or internal failure could lead to unathorised data disclosure, financial or data manipulation, critically affecting WMCA operations.

findings.headline: Wednesbury to Brierley Hill Metro Extension receives Reasonable Assurance from internal audit with six medium-risk recommendations

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: Wednesbury to Brierley Hill Metro Extension required governance simplification and accountability clarification, with eight remedial actions due September and October 2026
findings.detail: The WBHE audit received Reasonable Assurance but identified governance weaknesses. The report states: 'Improvement was required to simplify governance, clarify accountability and strengthen assurance, reporting, risk and information governance arrangements.' Eight management actions were agreed and are 'concentrated in September and October 2026' and should 'be incorporated promptly into the tracking process, with evidence of implementation and governance reset outcomes obtained'.
findings.matters: A major transport capital project requiring governance reset before delivery signals delivery complexity. Eight remedial actions compressed into two months indicates urgent governance remediation on active infrastructure delivery; material to capital delivery risk assessment.
findings.figures: 8 agreed actions; 0 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low priority recommendations; implementation due 30 Sep / 31 Oct 2026
findings.quote: Improvement was required to simplify governance, clarify accountability and strengthen assurance, reporting, risk and information governance arrangements. Management has agreed eight actions to strengthen programme governance, reporting, risk management and information governance. The actions are due mainly by 31 October 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Internal Audit Annual Outturn Report 2025/26 & Update Report
findings.headline: Multiple audit recommendations have moved beyond original delivery dates, including overdue actions on Longbridge Park & Ride, Change Control and Digital Transport Systems
findings.detail: The report states 'several older actions have moved beyond their original delivery dates, particularly in Longbridge Park & Ride, Change Control and the customer-facing digital transport systems review.' Specific examples include Longbridge P&R (decision on car park charging still outstanding), Change Control (training webinar outstanding), and Digital Transport Systems (actions running to October 2027). The report notes revised dates 'should remain credible and supported by clear ownership and evidence'.
findings.matters: Repeatedly revised and overdue audit recommendations indicate management is not implementing governance improvements promptly. For a lender or peer finance director, this suggests remediation of control weaknesses identified in previous audits is not being resourced or prioritised adequately.
findings.figures: Longbridge P&R due 31 Oct 2026; Change Control due 30 Nov 2026; Digital Transport Systems actions running to Oct 2027; 52 actions remain open across forward monitoring population
findings.quote: several older actions have moved beyond their original delivery dates, particularly in Longbridge Park & Ride, Change Control and the customer-facing digital transport systems review. Revised dates should remain credible and supported by clear ownership and evidence.

findings.matters: Cybersecurity governance is an emerging material risk as WMCA expands services through devolution. A Limited Assurance opinion with 10 remedial actions signals weaknesses in cyber governance that require urgent fixing; for a lender, this is material to operational resilience and regulatory compliance risk.

findings.paper_title: Revised Annual Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) Statement 2026-2027
findings.headline: Pre-2008 capital expenditure debt repayment timeline extends to 2051/52 under annuity-based MRP method
findings.detail: The authority applies MRP charges determined by the expected useful life of assets as principal repayment on an annuity with 2% annual interest rate, rather than as a percentage of the capital financing requirement. The final MRP provision on capital expenditure incurred before 1 April 2008 will be made in 2051/52.
findings.matters: Long-term debt repayment profiles affect a council's debt forecasting, financial planning headroom, and refinancing risk; lenders assess councils' ability to repay over extended timescales
findings.quote: Using this method the final provision will be made, on capital expenditure incurred prior to 1 April 2008, in 2051/52.

findings.paper_title: Revised Annual Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) Statement 2026-2027
findings.headline: Previous 2026/27 MRP statement contained an error in charging rate that has been corrected following independent review
findings.detail: The approved statement stated that charging would be determined as 2% of the capital financing requirement, but guidance allows 4%. An independent review found that percentage-based charging is not the most prudent method anyway, and the authority continues to use an annuity-based approach aligned with asset useful life instead. Using the percentage method would leave £37m of the remaining £103m pre-2008 CFR outstanding in 25 years and £13m in 50 years.
findings.matters: Shows compliance review processes working; lenders and peer councils watch how authorities catch and correct accounting errors and governance gaps
findings.figures: 2% vs 4% error; £37m of £103m outstanding in 25 years; £13m in 50 years under percentage method
findings.quote: The statement approved for 2026/2027 contained an error stating that charging 'will be determined as 2% of the capital financing requirement in respect of that expenditure.' The option available in the Guidance however is for charging to be determined as 4% of the capital financing requirement.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Government devolution announcement of 31 July 2026 pending clarification on fiscal devolution timetable and mechanics of income tax retention
findings.detail: Government announced proposals to shift powers from Whitehall to WMCA covering transport, housing, skills, regeneration and economic growth, including wider fiscal powers to retain and manage locally generated tax revenues. However, exact fiscal devolution timetable, mechanics of income tax retention and full scope of new powers still require clarification. Further clarity expected in Autumn through fiscal devolution roadmap. WMCA will assess implications for funding, governance and delivery once detailed guidance available.
findings.matters: Could significantly affect WMCA's future funding model, fiscal autonomy and financial sustainability; signals period of uncertainty in funding architecture; relevant to lenders assessing medium and long-term financial stability
findings.figures: No figures specified yet
findings.quote: Several elements of the announcement still require clarification, including the exact fiscal devolution timetable, the mechanics of income tax retention and the full scope of new powers that will be given to the WMCA. Further clarity is expected in the Autumn through the Government's fiscal devolution roadmap.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Pay agreement reached at 3.5% for staff and 3.3% for Chief Officers with commitment to implement higher National Joint Council settlement if agreed
findings.detail: WMCA agreed local pay increase of 3.5% backdated to 1 April 2026, with commitment to implement any higher NJC settlement if agreed nationally. This is first time WMCA has negotiated directly with regional and local unions rather than through Passenger Transport Forum. Settlement is within budget assumptions and balances employee support with affordability. Chief Officers awarded 3.3%. However, should final NJC award exceed 3.5%, this could create modest additional pressure in medium term financial plan.
findings.matters: Shows pay contained for 2026/27 but creates contingent liability if national settlement exceeds local rate; signals organisational change in pay negotiation approach; relevant to lenders assessing future cost pressures
findings.figures: 3.5% staff pay award, 3.3% Chief Officers
findings.quote: a pay agreement has been reached locally providing for a 3.5% increase, backdated to 1 April 2026, with a commitment to implement any higher National Joint Council (NJC) settlement if agreed nationally.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Total reserves forecast to decline by £10.5m to £359.9m with substantial unallocated capacity retained
findings.detail: Opening reserves of £370.4m forecast to reduce by £10.5m to £359.9m by 31 March 2027. Corporate and Strategic Resilience Reserves forecast to £55.8m with £53.8m uncommitted. Smoothing Reserve (largest reserve category) forecast to increase to £205.0m. Risk and Contingency Reserve stable at £40.1m with £2m uncommitted. Reserves are actively deployed to support approved priorities, transformation activity and financial resilience.
findings.matters: Lenders monitor reserve levels and deployment; despite planned drawdown, authority maintains substantial unallocated reserves for contingency; shows forward planning and active reserve management
findings.figures: Opening £370.4m, closing £359.9m, drawdown £10.5m; Corporate/Strategic £55.8m (£53.8m uncommitted); Smoothing £205.0m; Risk/Contingency £40.1m (£2m uncommitted)
findings.quote: the forecast position indicates a net use of approximately £10.5m of reserves during 2026/27, reducing total reserves from £370.4m at 1 April 2026 to an anticipated closing balance of £359.9 at 31 March 2027.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Bus Reform additional £2.0m professional advice costs approved and accommodated within Transport service underspends
findings.detail: Additional £2m for external professional advice to support bus reform was approved in July 2026. Rather than creating budget pressure, this is being absorbed through underspends identified elsewhere within Transport service, creating no net pressure on overall budget. Separately, £5.2m of planned reserve drawdown for Bus Reform has been rescheduled to 2027/28 following delivery profile review. Programme remains on track with no material change to overall costs or scope.
findings.matters: Shows Transport service managing additional approved costs within existing envelope despite complexity; improves this year's reserve position by deferring £5.2m drawdown to next year; demonstrates budget flexibility and financial management
findings.figures: £2.0m additional approved costs, £5.2m reserve drawdown rescheduled
findings.quote: an additional requirement of £2.0m for external professional advice to support the delivery of significant bus reform activity which was granted approval in July 2026. This additional expenditure is currently being accommodated through underspends identified elsewhere within the Transport service

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Capital programme delivered 19% of planned expenditure by end Q1 with 0.4% variance against forecast
findings.detail: £104.2m spent by end June 2026 of annual programme. Quarter 1 forecast of £558.1m against budget of £560.1m represents only £2.0m variance. Despite £33.3m rephasing adjustments, substantially offset by £26.8m acceleration in other areas. No significant affordability concerns. 81% of programme remains to be delivered, concentrated in 20 high-value schemes. Metro WM Heavy Rail Enhancement (£79.1m) and Metro Birmingham Eastside (£22.5m) are major infrastructure drivers.
findings.matters: Demonstrates strong delivery momentum and programme management across complex portfolio; maintains strategic investment pace on major economic infrastructure; indicates implementation capacity relevant to lenders assessing project delivery
findings.figures: £104.2m delivered (19%), £2.0m variance (0.4%), £558.1m forecast, £560.1m budget
findings.quote: The Quarter 1 capital forecast of £558.1m remains closely aligned to the latest 2026/27 Capital Programme budget of £560.1m, representing a variance of only £2.0m (0.4%) below plan.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Concessionary travel patronage declined from late 2025/26, creating £1.5m forecast saving as growth trend reverses
findings.detail: When budget was set, concessionary travel under ENCTS scheme was on sustained growth trend. Growth plateaued in late 2025/26 and has subsequently declined, resulting in lower costs than budgeted. Paper forecasts demand unlikely to return to growth levels experienced in early 2025/26. This £1.5m saving will continue to be monitored but represents reversal of earlier trajectory.
findings.matters: Signals reversal in usage pattern for subsidised bus travel; affects future cost projections and budget planning assumptions; relevant to peer councils making similar concessionary travel assumptions and to lenders assessing demand stability
findings.figures: £1.5m saving
findings.quote: patronage growth plateaued during the latter part of 2025/26 and has subsequently declined, resulting in lower costs than originally budgeted... the current assumption is that demand is unlikely to return to the levels experienced during the strongest growth periods of early 2025/26.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Local authority contribution of £1.5m to Business Rates Growth forecast undeliverable after Business Rates reset
findings.detail: Budget assumed £1.5m of Business Rates Growth income from local authority contributions. Latest information from authorities indicates growth is minimal following recent reset of Business Rates system, making this contribution unlikely to be achieved this year. Creates potential pressure against approved budget. Treasury Management income improvement will offset loss this year but signals structural change in funding base.
findings.matters: Represents structural shift in Business Rates funding model post-reset; affects sustainability of funding base in future years; relevant to lenders assessing income stability and peer councils facing same pressures
findings.figures: £1.5m unachievable contribution
findings.quote: the £1.5m contribution is unlikely to be deliverable during the current financial year, creating a potential pressure against the approved budget.

findings.paper_title: 2026/27 First Quarter Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Corporate income forecast to increase by at least £10.0m against approved budget, driven by stronger Treasury Management investment returns
findings.detail: Improvement primarily attributable to higher cash balances than originally forecast from additional grant funding, together with interest rates remaining higher than assumed. Paper explicitly states this improvement is largely one-off and should not be regarded as a recurring benefit that can be relied upon in future years. Position remains sensitive to macroeconomic conditions.
findings.matters: Shows improved cash position this year but signals significant headwind when Treasury returns normalize in future years; peer councils and lenders need to distinguish underlying operational position from treasury effects
findings.figures: £10.0m forecast increase
findings.quote: Early indications from the Quarter 1 revenue monitoring position suggest a forecast increase in corporate income of at least £10.0m against the approved 2026/27 budget. The favourable forecast is primarily attributable to stronger than anticipated Treasury Management investment returns, arising from higher cash balances than originally forecast

findings.paper_title: Appendix 10 - Compliance with Treasury and Prudential limits ( Quarter 1)
findings.headline: Forecast investments of £735m exceed external debt of £499m, creating a net investment position of £236m.
findings.detail: Investment balances exceed external borrowing by £236m as at Q1, compared to a budgeted -£121m net borrowing position for 2026/27. This stronger cash position reflects capital expenditure slippage, though it will likely narrow as capital projects progress.
findings.matters: Net investment position (more cash than debt) reduces immediate refinancing risk and strengthens creditworthiness, key metrics for lenders evaluating authority financial health.
findings.figures: Investments £735m actual vs £653m budget; External Debt £499m actual vs £532m budget; Net position -£236m actual vs -£121m budget
findings.quote: Net Borrowing – gross external debt less investment balances – is forecast to fall during the year as investment levels have risen as a consequence of capital expenditure slippage in 2025/26 and 2026/27 and Integrated Settlement grant allocation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 10 - Compliance with Treasury and Prudential limits ( Quarter 1)
findings.headline: Interest receivable on investments exceeds interest payable on debt, producing a financing cost ratio of -4.37%.
findings.detail: Investment interest earned on £735m exceeds debt service costs on £499m of borrowing, producing a negative financing cost ratio of -4.37%, meaning interest income benefits the revenue budget. This is better than the -1.97% budgeted for 2026/27.
findings.matters: A council where interest income exceeds interest costs has lower revenue pressure and improved financial resilience.
findings.figures: -4.37% (Q1 actual) versus -1.97% (2026/27 budget)
findings.quote: WMCA has a negative forecasted ratio for 2026/27 as interest receivable on investments exceeds interest payable on loans and Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP.)

findings.paper_title: Appendix 10 - Compliance with Treasury and Prudential limits ( Quarter 1)
findings.headline: Capital expenditure reached £104.2m in the first quarter of a £554m annual budget, reflecting ongoing capital programme slippage.
findings.detail: The authority spent £104.2m on capital projects in Q1, tracking at 18.8% of the 2026/27 budget. This reflects continuation of slippage from 2025/26, explicitly identified as the driver of higher cash balances and lower external borrowing than forecast.
findings.matters: Capital delivery slippage affects financing requirements, project completion timelines, and is a key metric peers and lenders monitor.
findings.figures: £554m 2026/27 budget, £104.2m Q1 actual
findings.quote: Net Borrowing – gross external debt less investment balances – is forecast to fall during the year as investment levels have risen as a consequence of capital expenditure slippage in 2025/26 and 2026/27 and Integrated Settlement grant allocation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 8 - Integrated Settlement Summary
findings.headline: Major programmes including Creative Growth, Investment Zone and Midlands Local Growth Company remain formally undefined as at June, with procurement activity ongoing
findings.detail: Several major programmes are described as still being formalised. Further procurement activity took place during Q2 2026/27, and the authority states this will provide a clearer picture of programme delivery and associated expenditure once finalised. This indicates project definition was not complete at the start of the financial year.
findings.matters: A finance director watching how peers manage grant-dependent programmes would note that key initiatives remain formally undefined mid-year, which could affect spending profiles, deliverability in the current year, and the robustness of budget forecasts.
findings.figures: Not specified
findings.quote: Some programmes and projects, including Creative Growth, the Investment Zone, and the Midlands Local Growth Company, are some part of projects are being formalised. Further procurement activity took place during Q2, and once finalised, this will provide a clearer picture of programme delivery and associated expenditure.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 8 - Integrated Settlement Summary
findings.headline: CRSTS capital and revenue approvals remain pending as at June 2026, totalling £6.68m in unfunded commitments
findings.detail: CRSTS1 revenue funding of £2.97m remains subject to formal approval, with clarity expected from Q2 forecasting. CRSTS2 revenue funding of £3.71m has not yet been formally approved and is not expected to be spent in 2026/27. Combined, these represent unconfirmed funding of £6.68m within the current spending envelope.
findings.matters: Mid-year funding approvals that remain pending create uncertainty about the actual spending baseline and potential cash-flow or borrowing implications if approvals are withheld or delayed further.
findings.figures: CRSTS1 £2.97m, CRSTS2 £3.71m
findings.quote: CRSTS1: £2.97m remains subject to formal approval. The Q2 forecast is expected to provide a clearer position and CRSTS2: £3.71m Funding has not yet been formally approved and is not expected to be spent in FY2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 8 - Integrated Settlement Summary
findings.headline: Capital programme carries forward £155m (67% of available budget) to 2027/28, largely due to CRSTS projects and Active Travel design stage gates not yet met
findings.detail: Of £235m capital available, only £15m has been spent as at June. The main carry-forward relates to CRSTS (City Region Sustainable Transport) projects which will be utilised once historic grants are fully deployed. Active Travel represents £7.28m forecast for 2027/28 spending, pending achievement of 75% design stage and OBC submission.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender would need to understand whether a 67% capital programme carry-forward represents normal grant-cycle timing or delivery risk, and whether design gate delays create cash-flow dependencies into the next financial year.
findings.figures: £235m available, £15m spent as at June 2026, £155m carry-forward to 2027/28, £7.28m Active Travel forecast 2027/28
findings.quote: The main carry-forward relates to CRSTS projects. This grant will be utilised once the historic grants have been fully utilised. The historic grants were not part of the IS Grant. Active Travel: £7.28m is forecast to be spent in FY2027/28. Funding is claimed one year in arrears following achievement of the 75% design stage and OBC submission, which is currently pending.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 6 - Investment Programme Commitments
findings.headline: Coventry Electric Bus City programme is 19% spent of its £5m approved budget as of June 2026
findings.detail: The programme shows actual spend of £954k against approved commitments of £5,000k. This is the largest underspend in the portfolio as a proportion of approved budget and suggests either delayed project start or stalled delivery.
findings.matters: Significant underspend relative to approval could indicate delivery delays or obstacles to project timescales, affecting the council's ability to deliver planned transport infrastructure within the anticipated financial envelope
findings.figures: £5,000k approved commitments; £954k actual spend
findings.quote: Coventry Electric Bus City5,000 954

findings.paper_title: Appendix 6 - Investment Programme Commitments
findings.headline: Regional Recovery & Risks programme exceeded approved budget of £26.2m by £624k as of June 2026
findings.detail: The programme recorded actual spend of £26,866k against approved commitments of £26,242k, making it the only programme in the portfolio to overspend its allocation. This represents a 2.4% overrun against budget.
findings.matters: Budget overruns indicate either scope creep or inadequate original budgeting, both of which signal budget control challenges and may require additional funding to complete
findings.figures: £26,242k approved commitments; £26,866k actual spend
findings.quote: Regional Recovery & Risks26,242 26,866
